newsitem.title: SPAIN: Washington should have delayed strike, Spain says.
newsitem.headline: Washington should have delayed strike, Spain says.

text.p: Spain, one of the United States' NATO allies, said on Tuesday it wished Washington had delayed its strike against Iraqi targets and declined to voice support for the attack.
Foreign Minister Abel Matutes, asked in a radio interview whether Madrid's official reaction was one of "understanding and support" for Washington's decision, replied:
"(Our reaction) is one of understanding, although we would have wanted that armed intervention to be, at least, postponed."

He did not elaborate on Spain's feelings but said the United States had told its allies late on Monday that it was about to launch the strike, which he described as aimed at an unspecified missile base.
Washington consulted Saudi Arabia, British Prime Minister John Major and French President Jacques Chirac before taking the final decision, Matutes told Ser radio.
Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar was going ahead with a scheduled trip to Latin America as there was no reason to change plans, the foreign minister added.
